about.text: Colby is a semihard orange cheese made from cow's milk. It is named after the U.S. city of Colby, Wisconsin, where it was first developed in 1885 and quickly became popular. Today the cheese is typically used in snacks, sandwiches, and salads.

how.label: cool the curd
how.text: Adding water to cool the stirred curd stops the pieces from matting together into slabs, the step that defines cheddaring. The pieces are then drained, salted and pressed, giving a cheese with up to 40% moisture.
